title: Policy ingestion linter and fallback suggestion pipeline for routing DSL
creator: Evelyn Zhang
description:
Background: As we migrate routing rules to the new declarative DSL, we need a robust multi-stage validation and suggestion pipeline that catches unsafe rules early, provides actionable error messages to users, and proposes fallback model variants and region-tier mappings automatically. This ticket implements an ingest-time linter + a lightweight suggestion engine used by the Console and the policy CI gate.

Goals:
- Two-pass validation: syntactic schema checks (strict) followed by semantic checks (best-effort) that surface ambiguous or potentially unsafe config combinations.
- Produce human-friendly diagnostics with remediation hints and links to design docs.
- Recommend fallback model variants and tier downgrades for cases where latency/capacity constraints or customer isolation policies are violated.
- Add a migration shim that emits deprecation warnings for legacy fields and auto-transforms safe subsets to the new typed IR.
- Integrate the linter with the rollout gate to block canary deploys with high-risk routing rules.

Non-goals: Completely replacing the runtime resolver (this ticket focuses on ingest-time tooling and developer UX).

Acceptance criteria:
- A set of unit tests covering schema, semantic rules, and suggested fallbacks.
- Console shows lint results inline when editing routes and includes actionable links.
- CI policy gate fails a sample unsafe manifest used by SRE playbook.
- Migration shim logged in the audit trail with explicit before/after examples in the PR.

Technical approach:
1) Schema layer: implement JSON Schema + typed extras (enums, constraints) converted into a lightweight typed AST. Fail fast for malformed fields.
2) Semantic pass: run a set of conflict detectors (region+tier mismatch, incompatible model variant + quantization profile, mutually exclusive fallback clauses). These produce WARNING or ERROR depending on severity.
3) Suggestion engine: for WARNING-level findings propose a ranked list of fallback actions (e.g., use model-4-compat instead of model-4-quantized, move region to eu-west-1 for data residency, fall back to standard tier with lower batch size). Suggestions include estimated delta on latency/cost when possible.
4) UI/Console contract: lint output must provide a stable suggestion-id so Console can render a single-click apply action that opens a PR or a migration preview.
5) CI integration: expose CLI exit codes and a --treat-warnings-as-errors flag for rollout gating.

Instrumentation and observability:
- Telemetry events: lint.invoked, lint.finding.{severity}, suggestion.applied. No PII.
- Add a dashboard for top lint failure types over the last 90 days.

Deliverables:
- backend service module: routing-lint-service (Scala) and typed AST definitions.
- CLI binary used in CI and by SRE.
- Console UI hook and a lightweight apply flow.
- Migration document and compatibility notes in Confluence.

Risks and mitigations:
- False positives blocking rollouts: start with warnings-only mode during canary period and gradually tighten to errors.
- Suggestion inaccuracies for cost/latency estimates: surface ranges and link to bench dashboard rather than absolute numbers.
- Performance overhead for ingest: keep lint asynchronous by default and run blocking checks only when --strict is set.
comments: 2026-02-19: Spike complete — parsed 500 existing routing manifests and categorized 37 unique schema violations. Most common issue: legacy 'region_hint' field conflicting with 'region_selector'. Saved sample data in drive: https://docs.redwood.ai/drive/smart-routing/spike-results

2026-02-25: Design review with Console team — agreed on suggestion-id contract and apply-preview UX. Action: Console to implement an apply-preview endpoint (PR draft: github.com/redwood/console/pull/842).

2026-03-03: Security reviewed quick-check; KMS/Auth not directly involved. Noted that lint telemetry must not contain customer tokens. Security asked for opt-out for telemetry per enterprise settings.

2026-03-08: PR opened for schema layer and typed AST: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/1912. Unit tests added for enum coercion and deprecation warnings. Requesting ENG review from @Nadia Ortiz and @Liam O'Connell.

2026-03-12: Integration smoke done on staging. Console shows inline lint messages for sample policy. Two outstanding TODOs: (1) add fallback ranking weights based on recent capacity metrics, (2) add CLI flag --treat-warnings-as-errors for rollout gate.
